*Speaking as the farmer:*

Aiya, another season. Same land, same crops — wheat then maize, like always. My man works in town most of the year so it's me and the older kids handling the fields. Twenty years I've been doing this, my hands know the work.

For the wheat I'll plant after the National Day holiday, around the time the cold comes in — maybe October 12, 13. I buy seed from the shop in town, the kind everyone around here uses, the shopkeeper tells me which one is good this year. Before plowing I spread the compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind in the blue bag — about one and a half bags per mu, that's what my mother-in-law taught me and what the neighbors do. Then in spring when the wheat starts standing up, I scatter urea, maybe half a bag per mu. If I put too little the wheat looks yellow and thin and the harvest is poor; better to put a bit extra than not enough.

Water the wheat three times — once before winter so it doesn't freeze dry, once at jointing in spring, once when the grain is filling. The well is shared, costs money for the electric, but if you don't water you get nothing. Last year I got about 400 kg per mu, year before a bit less because of that dry spring. I expect about the same this year.

After the wheat machine harvests in June, I have to move fast — maize must go in within days or it won't make it before frost. I buy hybrid maize seed, the Zhengdan kind or whatever is selling well. Same fertilizer routine, compound at planting and urea later when the maize is knee-high. Maize doesn't need as much water if the summer rains come, sometimes one watering, sometimes two.

For pests — I spray for weeds in the wheat field in spring with the herbicide, and for the maize I watch for borers. If I see them I spray, if not I save the money. My daughter-in-law helps with weeding by hand where the spray missed.

I don't have much cash so I count carefully. Whatever the off-farm money brings in goes mostly to fertilizer and the children. I don't try fancy things — what worked last year will work this year, the gods willing.
